title: ZipVoice long listening heats Xiaomi phones and drains battery quickly
symptom: The user reported fast heating and battery drain on Xiaomi 17 Pro at 1.45x with the screen on and no charging. A controlled 20-minute screen-on, unplugged 1.45x baseline on Xiaomi 15 Ultra also produced clear heating confirmed by the user's touch, substantial charge-counter loss and a supply gap. Subsequent hot-state 2x audio had repeated pauses. The two devices must not be treated as interchangeable acceptance evidence.
root_cause: Not established. A bounded simpleperf sample placed over 98% of sampled user-mode CPU in libonnxruntime.so, making native inference the main observed CPU cost. Missing internal symbols prevent separating necessary model computation from thread-pool waiting or spinning. App-level investigation found bounded preparation and no sustained work after pause/stop settled; these observations do not prove that all native work is necessary or that spinning causes the heating.
fix: No accepted thermal fix yet. Spinning-policy and longer-request trials lacked stable benefit. Candidate C only changes four threads to three; two emulator CPU screening rounds decreased cumulative app CPU with the original voice, model, steps and segmentation retained. Three related emulator playback/control regressions and bounded implementation review passed. First-audio timing fluctuated and real-device thermal, battery and hot 2x evidence are still required; see the plan for measurements and decisions.

Real-device temperature, charge-loss and playback criteria were frozen before candidate measurements. Follow the linked plan for conditions, tolerances and results instead of deriving acceptance from thread count, instantaneous CPU or single-segment latency.

The user requires desktop candidate preparation and related regressions first, then Goal pause. The phone has been returned. Do not use a phone again until the user agrees to the test duration and confirms starting; take a fresh backup then and never restore this round's old backup over newer books, settings or progress.
evidence: Conditions, original APK identity, sensor distinctions, the baseline table, frozen acceptance criteria, candidate decisions and primary-source comparisons are maintained in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-23-offline-listening-thermal.md.

Actual cold and hot 35-second recordings were independently transcribed and checked against source text without whole-sentence omission or repetition; proper-name homophones do not establish a speech defect. This bounded result does not establish arbitrary-text correctness.

Legado and wallabag use external Android TTS engines or HTTP audio rather than this app's bundled voice-cloning path. Their bounded queues, stale-callback rejection and audio reuse inform mechanisms, not a comparable power claim. Shorter reference audio remains untested; three-thread screening is emulator-only.
failed_attempts: Completely disabling intra/inter-op spinning is not the preferred candidate: emulator audio contained a 1.886-second supply gap, while the matched original APK also paused for 0.909 and 3.333 seconds and had a 6954ms generation outlier. These samples expose supply risk and environmental variation, not proof that disabling spinning caused a performance regression or improved energy use. Do not select this configuration from either isolated sample.

Session force_spinning_stop also failed to show a stable CPU saving across the two matched screening rounds. Do not promote it to a real-device thermal candidate using only the favorable round; the numerical comparison remains in the linked plan.

Combining the same 34-character and 36-character text into one 70-character request did not reduce cumulative CPU in either micro-sample round and increased first-audio latency. Normal punctuation and min_char_in_sentence=30 were preserved. Do not change product segmentation on an assumed fixed-cost saving; this bounded result does not reject every possible segmentation policy.
impact: Long-listening heat, battery loss and hot-state 2x continuity remain unresolved. The baseline supports prioritizing ORT costs over unrelated UI work, but only a valid future real-device comparison can establish practical improvement. Offline packaging, voice, selected speed and user data remain mandatory constraints.
